identity.title: Detection of Exocometary CO within the 440 Myr Old Fomalhaut Belt: A Similar CO+CO<SUB>2</SUB> Ice Abundance in Exocomets and Solar System Comets

paper_type_evidence.quote: We observed the Fomalhaut belt with the ALMA array using Band 6 receivers, allowing simultaneously a wide bandwidth for 1.3mm dust continuum imaging

evidence.quote: Fomalhaut, at a distance of 7.7 pc, is the nearest circumstellar disk where CO has been searched for by ALMA to date.
The nearby (cite: vanLeeuwen2007), 440$\pm$40 Myr-old (cite: Mamajek2012), A3V (cite: Gray1989) star Fomalhaut

question.value: Is there CO gas co-located with the Fomalhaut dust belt, is it exocometary, and what CO+CO2 ice mass fraction in exocomets does it imply?

evidence.quote: We here present the detection of CO J=2-1 emission co-located with dust emission from the cometary belt in the 440 Myr-old Fomalhaut system.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00966.S.
We observed the Fomalhaut belt with the ALMA array using Band 6 receivers

evidence.quote: we achieve a 5.4$\sigma$ detection

why_this_method.value: Spatial and spectral filtering boosts SNR of faint emission

evidence.quote: we obtain a spectrum which is free from noise originating from spectral channels as well as spatial locations where no CO emission is expected

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Primordial CO rejected: column densities insufficient for shielding

evidence.quote: we conclude that the observed CO cannot have survived since the protoplanetary phase

evidence.quote: given the low SNR levels, we cannot distinguish whether all of the emission originates from this wedge
